subject: Quick clarification about the feedback sheet
text: Dear Professor, I wanted to quickly clarify my earlier note about the seminar feedback sheet. I realize I may have sounded abrupt, especially since I know you are juggling several classes and grant deadlines. My team is trying to compare student comments across three sessions, and we would be grateful for a small favor: could you glance over the summary draft and mark only the statements that feel inaccurate, not rewrite them? That keeps the language authentic while helping us avoid overinterpreting one room. We can keep the original wording unless a student clearly misspells a word, and we will remove any identifiable details before circulation. If this does not fit your week, perhaps the doctoral assistant can flag the problematic lines instead, or we can schedule a ten-minute call. I also attached a short checklist so there is no pressure to spend too long. Thanks for considering it. I appreciate your guidance, and I apologize if the first message seemed rushed. If there are any terms in the sheet that seem too technical for a public-facing report, please tell me, because I would rather simplify those phrases than accidentally change the intent of the comments. I can also share the anonymized raw notes if that would make your review faster, and we can delete them afterward. The main thing is accuracy, not polish.
